Comment: Outside ROI (noROI(input)). Extracts basic visual features (edges orientation color) in early visual areas. Handles initial processing of visual stimuli necessary for Perceptual Speed.
Output Semantics: Early-Visual-Features codes basic visual features extracted from retinal input (orientation spatial frequency color edges);

Comment: Outside ROI (noROI(input/output)). Codes category-specific high-level visual representations such as letters numbers objects. Bidirectionally connected with IPS via IPS-FG fiber tract. Provides visual category information for comparison to IPS and receives top-down modulation from IPS.
Output Semantics: High-Level-Visual-Representation codes category-specific visual representations such as letters numbers objects;

Names: MT/MST (Middle Temporal and Medial Superior Temporal Areas)
Comment: Outside ROI (noROI(input)). Processes visual motion information and projects to VIP LIP MIP in IPS. Provides temporal change information necessary for comparison of dynamic stimuli.
Output Semantics: Motion-Processing codes temporal change information such as motion direction speed trajectory of visual stimuli;

Comment: Outside ROI (noROI(input)). Provides attention modulation and contextual signals to IPS. Adjusts attention allocation to visual stimuli and supports rapid comparison processing.
Output Semantics: Thalamic-Attention-Hub codes attention priority to visual stimuli and contextual modulation signals;

Comment: Inside ROI. Integrates visual information from early visual areas (V1/V2) and high-level visual areas (Fusiform Gyrus). Constructs feature representations of visual stimuli and prepares input for comparison processing.
Output Semantics: Visual-Input-Integration codes unified representations of visual stimuli with integrated multi-layered visual features;
Requirement: U.Visual-Input-Integration receives inputs: U.Early-Visual-Features (basic visual features) U.High-Level-Visual-Representation (category-specific visual representations such as letters numbers objects) U.Thalamic-Attention-Hub (attention priority to visual stimuli and contextual modulation signals) and U.Top-Down-Attention-Control (attention control signals and decision criteria based on task demands). These are integrated to generate output: U.Visual-Input-Integration (unified representations of visual stimuli with integrated multi-layered features). This unified representation provides comprehensive descriptions of visual stimuli necessary for subsequent comparison processing.
Requirement realization by interface: The interface is (U.Pattern-Comparison U.Working-Memory-Maintenance) = U.Visual-Input-Integration(U.Early-Visual-Features U.High-Level-Visual-Representation U.Thalamic-Attention-Hub U.Top-Down-Attention-Control). As inputs it receives basic visual features from U.Early-Visual-Features category representations from U.High-Level-Visual-Representation attention modulation signals from U.Thalamic-Attention-Hub and task control signals from U.Top-Down-Attention-Control. By integrating these it outputs U.Visual-Input-Integration (unified visual representation) to both U.Pattern-Comparison and U.Working-Memory-Maintenance. The input-output relationship described in the Requirement is consistent with the Interface.
Capability: Receives as inputs low-level visual features (edges orientation color) and high-level category representations attention modulation signals and cognitive control signals; weights and integrates these and projects them into a single multidimensional representation space. This processing combines hierarchical feedforward integration with attention-driven dynamic weighting. In rapid comparison tasks such as Perceptual Speed selective attention allocation to task-relevant features determines integration efficiency. Neural basis: Posterior parietal cortex functions as a core hub integrating visual information for action control through hierarchical feedforward mechanisms (Gamberini et al. 2024; Plos Biology 2023). Superficial layers of visual cortex create a saliency map which feeds forward to parietal cortex. According to Integrated Information Theory PPC functions as a core complex of information integration (Frontiers in Neuroscience 2025).
Mechanism: Hierarchical feedforward integration: Low-level visual features (from V1/V2) and high-level category representations (from Fusiform Gyrus) project to different cortical layers within posterior IPS. These inputs are dynamically gated by attention signals (from Pulvinar). Top-down control signals (from dlPFC) adjust weighting toward task-relevant features. Integration is realized by combining inputs from multiple visual sources into a single high-dimensional representation space. In this space visual stimuli are represented as multidimensional vectors with each dimension corresponding to different visual features (both low-level and high-level). Attention-based weighting acts as multiplicative gain amplifying representation strength of task-relevant features.
Implementation: U.Visual-Input-Integration = α₁·U.Early-Visual-Features + α₂·U.High-Level-Visual-Representation where α₁ and α₂ are attention-based weighting coefficients: α₁ = f(U.Thalamic-Attention-Hub U.Top-Down-Attention-Control) α₂ = g(U.Thalamic-Attention-Hub U.Top-Down-Attention-Control) f g are nonlinear gain functions dependent on attention signals (e.g. sigmoid functions)

Comment: Inside ROI. Executes relational coding and similarity comparison of visual patterns. Core UC responsible for comparing presented stimuli to each other or to remembered stimuli. Includes two compartments LIPv and LIPd.
Output Semantics: Pattern-Comparison codes similarity distances and differences between visual patterns (comparison results);
Requirement: U.Pattern-Comparison receives inputs: U.Visual-Input-Integration (unified representations of visual stimuli with integrated multi-layered features) U.Working-Memory-Maintenance (memory representations of visual stimuli maintained in short-term) U.Motion-Processing (temporal change information such as motion direction speed trajectory) and U.Thalamic-Attention-Hub (attention priority and contextual modulation signals). It computes similarity distances between these visual representations and generates output: U.Pattern-Comparison (encoding of similarity distances and differences between visual patterns). This comparison processing quantifies similarity/difference between multiple presented stimuli or between presented and remembered stimuli.
Requirement realization by interface: The interface is (U.Comparison-Decision U.Oculomotor-Control) = U.Pattern-Comparison(U.Visual-Input-Integration U.Working-Memory-Maintenance U.Motion-Processing U.Thalamic-Attention-Hub). As inputs it receives current visual representations from U.Visual-Input-Integration memory representations from U.Working-Memory-Maintenance motion information from U.Motion-Processing and attention modulation from U.Thalamic-Attention-Hub. Using these it executes similarity comparison and outputs comparison results to U.Comparison-Decision and oculomotor signals to U.Oculomotor-Control. The input-output relationship described in the Requirement is consistent with the Interface.
Capability: Computes similarity distances between multiple high-dimensional visual representation vectors. This computation uses relational coding to construct a similarity distance matrix between visual patterns. The similarity metric can be dynamically adjusted according to task demands including selective weighting for specific visual feature dimensions (shape color category etc). This function also considers temporal asymmetry between patterns distinguishing similarity between current stimuli and past/future stimuli. Neural basis: High-order visual cortex uses relational coding (comparison of similarity distances) as the primary neural code (Nature Communications 2025). Lateral parietal cortex uses temporal asymmetry of neural pattern similarity to make recognition memory decisions (Nature Communications 2025). LIP executes relational coding of visual patterns supporting similarity comparison. Integrating multiple complementary representational similarity metrics (geometry unit-level tuning linear decodability) reveals sharper regional discrimination and hierarchical organization (arXiv 2024).
Mechanism: Similarity computation via relational coding: Neuronal populations within LIP represent visual stimuli as points in a high-dimensional space. Similarity comparison is realized by computing distances (e.g. Euclidean distance Mahalanobis distance) between these points. LIP constructs a similarity distance matrix within the visual representation space encoding which stimulus pairs are most similar/different. Temporal integration enables comparison of current visual input (from U.Visual-Input-Integration) and remembered stimuli (from U.Working-Memory-Maintenance) within the same representation space. Attention signals (from U.Thalamic-Attention-Hub) adjust weighting toward specific feature dimensions promoting task-relevant similarity judgments. Motion information (from U.Motion-Processing) enables comparison of temporally changing stimuli.
Implementation: U.Pattern-Comparison = d(U.Visual-Input-Integration U.Working-Memory-Maintenance) where d is a weighted distance function: d(x y) = √(Σᵢ wᵢ(xᵢ - yᵢ)²) wᵢ is the weight for feature dimension i adjusted by U.Thalamic-Attention-Hub. Integration of motion information: U.Pattern-Comparison(t) = ∫ d(U.Visual-Input-Integration(τ) U.Working-Memory-Maintenance) · κ(t-τ U.Motion-Processing) dτ where κ is the temporal integration kernel

Comment: Inside ROI. Maintains representations of remembered visual stimuli. Receives feedback from FEF and integrates memory information with current visual input to enable comparison.
Output Semantics: Working-Memory-Maintenance codes memory representations of visual stimuli maintained in short-term;
Requirement: U.Working-Memory-Maintenance receives inputs: U.Visual-Input-Integration (unified representations of visual stimuli) U.Oculomotor-Control (oculomotor commands and gaze position feedback information) and U.Top-Down-Attention-Control (attention control signals and decision criteria based on task demands). It maintains representations of visual stimuli for a short period (several seconds) and generates output: U.Working-Memory-Maintenance (memory representations of visual stimuli maintained in short-term). This memory representation functions as a reference stimulus for comparison with current visual input.
Requirement realization by interface: The interface is (U.Pattern-Comparison) = U.Working-Memory-Maintenance(U.Visual-Input-Integration U.Oculomotor-Control U.Top-Down-Attention-Control). As inputs it receives visual representations from U.Visual-Input-Integration oculomotor feedback from U.Oculomotor-Control and cognitive control signals from U.Top-Down-Attention-Control. By integrating these it maintains memory representations and outputs them to U.Pattern-Comparison. The input-output relationship described in the Requirement is consistent with the Interface.
Capability: Maintains high-dimensional visual representations in transformed formats for short periods. This maintenance is not a direct copy of sensory representations during perception but rather representations transformed and refined according to task goals. The maintenance mechanism combines sustained activity via recurrent neural circuits with inter-areal reverberation. Oculomotor feedback updates spatial coordinates of memory representations (coordinate transformation) and top-down control adjusts preferential maintenance of task-relevant information. When multiple information streams are maintained in parallel representations are orthogonalized to minimize interference. Neural basis: Posterior parietal cortex and occipitotemporal cortex maintain transformed representations different from perception during visual working memory (eNeuro 2025). PPC orthogonalizes representations of different information streams in VWM enabling adaptive visual processing (PMC 2024). Large-scale network models show memory states are sustained through inter-areal reverberation (UvA 2022). Recurrent on-center off-surround neural networks with distance-dependent inhibition can model VWM (Nature Scientific Reports 2025). Task-driven transformed account better explains VWM (Nature Communications 2024).
Mechanism: Maintenance of transformed representations: Visual input (from U.Visual-Input-Integration) is transformed according to task goals. This transformation suppresses task-irrelevant information and amplifies task-relevant information. The transformed representation is maintained by recurrent neural circuits within dorsal LIP (LIPd). Recurrent connections (excitatory and inhibitory) support sustained neuronal activity stabilizing memory representations for several seconds. Oculomotor feedback (from U.Oculomotor-Control) enables transformation from retinotopic to craniocentric coordinates keeping memory representations stable during eye movements. Top-down control (from U.Top-Down-Attention-Control) performs selective enhancement and gating of memory representations. When multiple memory items exist representations are orthogonalized in high-dimensional space avoiding interference.
Implementation: U.Working-Memory-Maintenance(t) = ∫₀ᵗ R(t-τ) · T(U.Visual-Input-Integration(τ)) · G(U.Top-Down-Attention-Control(τ)) dτ + β·U.Oculomotor-Control(t) where R(t) is the recurrent maintenance function (e.g. exponential decay e^(-t/τ_decay)) T(·) is the task-driven transformation function G(·) is the gate control function (values from 0 to 1) β is the coordinate transformation coefficient for oculomotor feedback. Orthogonalization (for multiple items): U.Working-Memory-Maintenanceᵢ ⊥ U.Working-Memory-Maintenanceⱼ for i ≠ j

Comment: Inside ROI. Integrates results of comparison processing and makes decisions about similarity/difference. Outputs decision signals through strong connections with prefrontal cortex.
Output Semantics: Comparison-Decision codes binary decision signals indicating whether visual stimuli are similar or different;
Requirement: U.Comparison-Decision receives inputs: U.Pattern-Comparison (encoding of similarity distances and differences between visual patterns) and U.Top-Down-Attention-Control (attention control signals and decision criteria based on task demands). It compares similarity distances with decision criteria and generates output: U.Comparison-Decision (binary decision signals indicating whether visual stimuli are similar or different). This decision signal is sent to prefrontal cortex and converted to final behavioral output (e.g. pressing same or different button).
Requirement realization by interface: The interface is (U.Decision-Output U.High-Level-Visual-Representation) = U.Comparison-Decision(U.Pattern-Comparison U.Top-Down-Attention-Control). As inputs it receives comparison results from U.Pattern-Comparison and decision criteria from U.Top-Down-Attention-Control. By integrating these it makes binary decisions and outputs decision signals to U.Decision-Output and visual modulation signals to U.High-Level-Visual-Representation. The input-output relationship described in the Requirement is consistent with the Interface.
Capability: Threshold decision function that converts continuous similarity distances into binary decisions (similar/different). This function implements an evidence accumulation mechanism such as the drift-diffusion model. Information about similarity distance is accumulated over time and a decision is made when a decision boundary is reached. Decision criteria (threshold) are dynamically adjusted according to task demands speed-accuracy tradeoff and prior probabilities. Anterior IPS integrates decision formation and cognitive control through strong coupling with prefrontal cortex. Neural basis: Anterior IPS (IPS3-4) is strongly connected with prefrontal areas and involved in decision processing (Greenberg et al. 2012; Basti et al. 2022). Parietal cortex accumulates sensory evidence to form decisions (drift-diffusion model). Image-computable models model rapid decision-making processes from visual input to decision (eLife 2024).
Mechanism: Evidence accumulation and threshold decision: Similarity distance information from U.Pattern-Comparison is temporally accumulated within anterior IPS. When accumulated evidence reaches a decision boundary (threshold) a binary decision (similar or different) is made. The decision boundary is dynamically adjusted by signals from U.Top-Down-Attention-Control. In tasks emphasizing speed the threshold is set low while in tasks emphasizing accuracy the threshold is set high. When a decision is made a decision signal is sent to prefrontal cortex (U.Decision-Output) and simultaneously a top-down visual modulation signal is sent to ventral visual stream (U.High-Level-Visual-Representation). This feedback enhances visual representations related to the decision optimizing subsequent processing.
Implementation: Evidence accumulation (drift-diffusion process): dE/dt = μ·U.Pattern-Comparison + σ·η(t) where E: accumulated evidence μ: drift rate (conversion rate from similarity distance to decision) σ: noise intensity η(t): Gaussian noise. Decision rule: U.Comparison-Decision = {similar if E(t) ≥ θ_upper; different if E(t) ≤ θ_lower}. Decision boundaries: θ_upper = f(U.Top-Down-Attention-Control) θ_lower = -f(U.Top-Down-Attention-Control) where f is the decision criteria adjustment function

Comment: Outside ROI (noROI(input)). Sends top-down attention control signals to IPS. Controls which stimulus features to attend to enhancing efficiency of comparison processing.
Output Semantics: Top-Down-Attention-Control codes attention control signals and decision criteria based on task demands;

Comment: Outside ROI (noROI(input/output)). Controls eye movements. Receives input from LIPv executes eye movements and sends feedback to LIPd. Controls attention shifts and gaze movements between visual stimuli.
Output Semantics: Oculomotor-Control codes oculomotor commands and gaze position feedback information;

Comment: Outside ROI (noROI(output)). Receives motor commands from VIP and AIP and prepares for response execution. Motor response output (button press etc) in Perceptual Speed tasks.
Outside ROI (noROI(output)). Receives decision signals from anterior IPS and makes final judgments. Converts similarity/difference judgment results to behavioral output.
